# PPTX experiment fixtures

English reading copy of [the original fixture notes](README.md). The metadata-cleanup section below is translated from Chinese; this copy records no new test run. Historical hashes refer to the files used in the original evidence, not this translation.

Every presentation is synthetic. No personal documents, sealed evaluation material, upstream Lab code or model calls were used.

- `basic-source.pptx`: generated titles, body paragraphs, Chinese, emoji, two notes pages and a hidden slide. Presentation order reverses the slide-part filenames. `expected.txt` is the exact output, including generated slide/role labels and no trailing LF.
- `rich-source.pptx`: the same text plus a blue synthetic PNG, chart, table, fade transition and title animation. `powerpoint-animation.xml` is the timing subtree of our own synthetic title Fade saved by PowerPoint 16.78, targeting shape 2. The generator reads it; no third-party implementation is involved.
- `powerpoint-basic-v1.pptx`: actual PowerPoint 16.78 GUI Save As. `powerpoint-basic-v2.pptx`: separate Save As followed by an actual notes edit and ordinary Save. `expected-v2.txt` contains the single changed note.
- `powerpoint-rich.pptx`: actual save following the initial synthetic timing repair and addition of a real Fade animation through the Animations ribbon. This repair is retained as a failure of the first synthetic generator, not presented as clean-source interoperability.
- `powerpoint-rich-clean.pptx`: corrected rich source opened without a repair prompt, saved through PowerPoint, closed and reopened without repair. Text, notes, hidden slide, picture, chart, table, transition and animation are retained.
- `powerpoint-layout.json`: original/fixture hashes and allowed changed byte ranges for all four actual saves. Only author/last-editor fields inside core.xml's Deflate payload and its local/central CRCs changed. Packed/unpacked lengths, ZIP layout and all other entry bytes are identical. The existing DOCX `scrub_word_fixture.py` is reused unchanged. Original saves stay outside Git at `<HOME>/Developer/Traeva-E-pptx-evidence/`.
- `validation.json`: source hashes, results, budgets, original failures and integration boundaries. This is developer evidence, not Codex-R or student acceptance.

Generate synthetic sources with Python 3, python-pptx 1.0.2 and Pillow:

```sh
python3 crates/traeva-core/tests/pptx_reader/make_fixture.py
```

Binary bytes can differ on regeneration due to ZIP timestamps; expected stored text and unsupported categories are fixed. Golden actual PowerPoint fixtures are not regenerated by this script. The initial invalid rich source is preserved locally as `rich-source-initial-invalid.pptx`; its empty p:tnLst triggered PowerPoint repair. Corrected fixtures use the actual saved timing subtree.

All actual saves return Partial, including basic v1/v2 because their packages hold dynamic fields. A picture-only presentation returns Unsupported rather than making generated slide labels count as retained source text.

## Author metadata cleanup

The student requested that the author fields in the four `powerpoint-*.pptx` saved packages be set to `Traeva synthetic`, that Company and Manager be cleared, and that all parts be checked for account information and machine-local paths. Ownership of the original fields was not confirmed. The student chose uniform cleanup; this does not establish whose identity those fields represented.

Eight occurrences were found; none remained after cleanup. ZIP entry order, compression methods and the decompressed bytes of every part except core.xml and app.xml stayed unchanged. Expected body text stayed unchanged. The current files are post-processed versions of existing real PowerPoint saves, not a new PowerPoint save or GUI verification.

`metadata-cleanup.json` records the fixed main baseline, original and cleaned package hashes, and checks. The four fixture hashes and sizes in `validation.json` were updated to the cleaned packages; the original save, layout and UI records remain historical evidence. Originals remain in Git history. The student decides whether that history needs separate treatment; this cleanup did not rewrite history or R3's original evidence.
